title: Sonny and the Creek Lullaby | Bedtime Story
description: Sonny the quokka follows a gentle bubbling sound through the Australian bush until she finds a sweet little creek, and lets its soft, steady music carry her all the way to sleep. A slow and soothing story from Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales.
narration:
As the afternoon light turned soft and orange, Sonny the quokka heard something.

It wasn't loud. It was very, very quiet — a small, steady sound coming from somewhere through the trees. A soft bubbling and trickling, like something whispering to itself.

Sunny tilted her little round ears and listened. She had never noticed that sound before. She padded softly through the bush, following it.

The ferns grew greener. The air felt cooler. And then, around a bend in the path, she found it — a small, clear creek, winding through the stones and roots of the bush.

The water moved so gently over the round smooth pebbles. Bubble, trickle, murmur. It never stopped, not even for a moment. Just a steady, soft, endless song.

Sunny sat down on a mossy bank right beside the water, close enough to feel the cool air rising from it. She listened. Really listened.

The creek didn't need to be loud to be lovely. It just kept going, steady and calm, like breathing. Like the whole bush was breathing slowly in and out.

Sunny's own breathing slowed down to match it. Her little shoulders softened. Her eyes grew heavy and still.

The light faded to deep blue. The stars appeared, one by one, and their reflections danced softly in the dark, quiet water.

Sunny let the sound of the creek fill her up — all the way to the edges, all the way to sleep.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, little creek. Goodnight, little one.
